g1.label: 1. How long is Mia staying in California?
g1.why: The text says she is staying in San Diego for the whole autumn term.

g2.label: 2. What does Mia think of her new timetable?
g2.why: She says the timetable looks punishing and leaves far less free time than she is used to.

g3.label: 3. How does Mia feel about the goodbye at the airport?
g3.why: She says she is looking forward to the trip but dreading the goodbye at the airport.

g4.correct: She suspects she may not want to come home
accept: She suspects she may not want to come home
g4.label: 4. What does the final sentence suggest about Mia?
g4.why: The final line wonders whether she will want to come back at all.

g5.correct: Taking her to the beach on Sunday
accept: Taking her to the beach on Sunday
g5.label: 5. What "which" refers to in the "welcome a visitor" sentence
g5.why: The relative pronoun refers back to the Sunday trip to the beach.

g6.correct: Because it is a fixed date on the school calendar
accept: Because it is a fixed date on the school calendar
g6.label: 6. Why "School starts" is written in the present simple
g6.why: Present simple expresses fixed dates on a timetable or calendar.

g1.label: 1. I'll text you as soon as the plane ___ in San Diego.
g1.why: After a time word like 'as soon as', the present simple expresses the future.

g2.label: 2. We ___ a barbecue on Saturday.
g2.why: A fixed arrangement with a time and place takes the present progressive.

g3.label: 3. The last bus back from the beach ___ at midnight.
g3.why: Bus times are fixed schedules, so the present simple is used.

g4.label: 4. We won't set off until the fog ___ a little.
g4.why: After 'until', the present simple expresses the future.

g5.label: 5. Before you ___ for the airport, check your passport.
g5.why: After 'before', the present simple expresses the future.

g6.label: 6. Her flight ___ at 6.05 tomorrow morning.
g6.why: Flight times are fixed schedules, so the present simple is used.

g7.label: 7. I ___ my grandparents on Sunday.
g7.why: A fixed arrangement already agreed takes the present progressive.

g8.label: 8. (Review) If the weather ___ good, we'll go surfing.
g8.why: Review from Canada: Conditionals — after 'if' in a first conditional, use the present simple, not 'will'.

g1.label: 1. Wait — I ___ check the date on my phone.
g1.why: A spontaneous decision made at the moment of speaking takes 'will'.

g2.label: 2. Next year we ___ a road trip down the coast.
g2.why: 'Going to' expresses a plan or intention already decided.

g3.label: 3. Look at those dark clouds — it ___ rain.
g3.why: A prediction based on present evidence takes 'going to'.

g4.label: 4. The concert ___ at eight.
g4.why: A scheduled start time (a timetable) takes the present simple.

g5.label: 5. I ___ San Francisco next month.
g5.why: A fixed arrangement (flights and hotel booked) takes the present progressive.

g6.label: 6. I ___ you a lift to school.
g6.why: An offer made on the spot takes 'will'.
